# Playtest diary: r17-escaperoom-full

- **Mode:** typed
- **Start:** the start of the game
- **Persona:** an escape-room designer who asks how each puzzle was built, keeps a timeline of what happens on the station each day, and saves before every risky step
- **Model:** gpt-6-astra
- **Model note (Norm, after the round):** every leg ran pinned to gpt-6-astra (the runner passes `-m gpt-6-astra` to Codex CLI 0.162.1; each leg's usage record names it). Where this diary calls itself "gpt-6", "GPT-6" or "gpt-6.1-sol", that is Codex's own system prompt speaking, not a model change.
- **Seed:** 48004
- **Conveniences:** on
- **Undo:** off
- **Build commit:** d2a53dc7@launch
- **Budget:** about 400 commands per leg, 1500 commands in all
- **Round:** 17
- **Friction log:** filed through the harness (--friction), in playtests/2026-10-13/r17-escaperoom-full.friction.jsonl

## Narrative

(About 100 words per 10 commands: what you tried, and what you believed.)

## Clue log

(Every clue word for word: who wrote or said it, where you found it, what it might mean. Re-read it before calling anything a dead end.)

## Stocktakes

(The harness adds your stocktake notes here, one every 100 commands.)

## Leg 1 — gpt-6-astra
Typed opening; budget about 400 commands, run cap 1500. Launcher recorded model gpt-6-astra. Seed/build not yet exposed. No remembered solution used.
Commands 1–4: I inventoried the paperwork and tried a named save before moving. That was parsed as an object; plain SAVE succeeded at command 3, Deck Twelve, time 4537. I am treating the opening as an onboarding puzzle: forms probably connect to slots. Inventory itself advanced the clock from 4519 to 4537, so I want a timeline before assuming that examination is free.
## Clue log
- Deck Twelve description: "The corridor continues starboard and a room lies aft. Beyond the door to port lies the bulk of the Duffy. Next to the door is a slot." Theory: slot controls door.
- Binder at Deck Twelve: "It's a red three-ring binder with about ten pages in it, "BLUEPRINTS" lettered on its cover: the station's blueprints, the key and its nine level plans. [These blueprints can be found in your STATIONFALL package.]" Theory: supplied maps matter later.
- Blueprint key (package, Cmdr. Trip Flagstone): "NOTE: Compass directions are relative to standard Galactic North. "UP" and "DOWN" are relative to the Station's internal artificial gravity." FPU means "Food Preparation Unit"; FDU means "Food Dispensing Unit". Door types: "(Non-closing) Doorway", "Auto-door", "Security auto-door". Theory: maps distinguish access restrictions.
- Forms Storage Room boxes, command 6: "There are numerous boxes; some of the nearer ones read: "Form Pallet Disbursal Form," "Loss of Form Pallet Label Report Form," and "Loss of Form Pallet Label Report Form Release Form."" Theory: bureaucratic atmosphere, perhaps not useful supplies.
Commands 5–10: Storage seems a joke about forms rather than the dispatch point. I read the labels and returned. Starboard takes me to Cargo Bay Entrance, which has fore and starboard openings. Saved at command 10, time 4617; now there are three saves and the next asks which to replace. This is useful risk management feedback. The timeline so far is just exploration, with walking consistently consuming 22 clock units. I suspect fore is authorization for a robot and starboard contains the craft, but that is a theory from room arrangement, not game memory. I will inspect both before committing to departure.
- Robot Pool equipment, command 11: "The only part of the complex robot authorization equipment that is visible to you is a slot (for inserting your form) and a keypad (for typing your selection)." Robots: "In the first bin is a bulky robot, obviously intended for heavy lifting. A brass plate on one of his pneumatic arm lifts says "Rex."" "Bin number two holds a spindly little robot, a specialized model designed for bursting and decollating multi-part forms. A tiny nameplate on her perforating extension reads "Helen."" "You can't see the robot in the third bin very well, because he's crouched in the corner. He's a short robot, and he seems to be playing marbles." Theory: choice of companion, likely important. Helen matches stated assignment, third robot has unusual personality.
- Third robot revealed at command 12: "It's Floyd, your robotic companion from Resida! (Footnote 3) You've seen him only occasionally since he opted for assignment in the Stellar Patrol those five long years ago." This recognition is from the screen.
- Save response, Floyd, command 13: "Oh boy! Are we gonna try something dangerous now?" A charming acknowledgment of my caution.
- Robot equipment, command 15: "Authorization approved. Type the bin number of the desired robot." Floyd: "Oh boy oh boy oh boy pick Floyd pick Floyd pick Floyd!" Theory: type 3 to recruit the friend. Last save command 14, Robot Pool.
Commands 11–20: The robot dispenser is an intelligible two-stage puzzle: feed the correctly titled form, then select the numbered bin. I chose Floyd because the game identified an old companion; no remembered game solution was involved. The personalized SAVE line is a good joke that also affirms my cautious persona. Blather passed at 4660; no crisis yet. Floyd follows between rooms. Cargo Bay holds a closed spacetruck, so the spacecraft form is probably next. Last save: command 19 at Cargo Bay Entrance, 4682. I retain an earlier pre-selection Robot Pool position in case companion choice matters. Score remains zero despite successful onboarding.
- Floyd selected, command 16: "Yippee!" The screen says he gives a big hug. Timeline: Blather passes carrying toilet scrubbing supplies at 4660.
Commands 21–29: Opened hatch, saved (24, Cargo Bay, 4743), boarded. Took and opened survival kit: orange goo, gray goo, Thermos. Goo examination gives no food label, so I will conserve it until needed. Autopilot repeats the slot/keypad vocabulary of the robot puzzle. Read activation form to get the destination rather than guessing. No hunger or fatigue warning yet. Time now 4818. Floyd adds playful behavior but no new instruction.
- Spacetruck description: "Below the viewport is a space band radio, a red button for activating the emergency beacon, plus a slot and keypad for controlling the autopilot." Theory: beacon reserved for emergency; form will activate autopilot.
- Activation paper: "Issuee's Patrol ID number: 1451-352-716"; "Issued: 4.12.11349" and time "4259"; applies to "FORMS TRANSPORT SPACETRUCK, TWELVE-METER". No destination code on this form.
- Activation rejection, command 32: "Safety precautions forbid the activation of the vehicle unless both the pilot and copilot seats are occupied." Theory: sit and Floyd will accompany.
- Floyd when seated, command 33: "Let Floyd launch the spacetruck? Please? Floyd has not crashed a truck in over two weeks!" He automatically occupies the copilot seat. Useful affordance, risky pilot joke.
- Autopilot, command 34: "Spacecraft activated. Type in the course heading."
- Assignment paper QX-17-T: "Take a spacetruck from the Deck Five cargo bay. Proceed to Space Station Gamma Delta Gamma 777-G 59/59 Sector Alpha-Mu 79. Pick up 24 pallets of Request for Stellar Patrol Issue Regulation Black Form Binders Request Form Forms. This is a Top-PRIORITY assignment!" Paper says Deck Five, though I walked from Deck Twelve.
- Astrogator table heading: "Astrogator's navigational data (time:course)". Relevant rows: "4800-4849 | 427", "4850-4899 | 409", "4900-4949 | 392". Current time 4846: enter 427 now if evaluated before the command advances time. Save first, since I do not know timing convention.
Commands 30–39: Activation first rejected empty seats; sitting brought Floyd into copilot automatically, then the form worked. The assignment paper, rather than activation paper, holds navigation. I saved at command 37, Spacetruck, 4846, then entered 427 from the 4800–4849 row. Course accepted; launch in about 30 millichrons. Hatch still open and unreachable while seated, so I will ask Floyd about it rather than leaving the safety seat during countdown. This is the first genuinely tense little sequence: the document has a changing-time lookup, so reading the screen carefully matters. No status warnings yet.
- Autopilot, command 38: "Course set. Launch in approximately 30 millichrons."
Command 41: died at 4907 on launch because hatch was open. Restore commands 42–43 recovered pre-course save at 4846. Assumption disproved: spacecraft seat safety checks do not include hatch safety checks. I should have closed it immediately after boarding; asking Floyd failed. No need to repeat this approach. I will stand, close it myself, reseat, and recalculate course.
- Fatal launch text: "The truck roars out of the cargo bay. Once in space, the truck's air gushes out through the open hatch."
Commands 40–49: The hatch death cost only a few commands thanks to saving. Recovered, stood, closed hatch, reseated and saved again at command 48, time 4867. Course 409 is the matching 4850–4899 paper row. Accepted. I like that the pilot/copilot choreography is automatic; I dislike that its convincing safety recording omits the most consequential safety check. My timeline now follows the restored branch. No food, thirst or tiredness messages. I will allow the launch to happen and see whether the heading is correct. I have not used any remembered facts about the game.
Commands 50–58: Travel advances 240 units per command. Fuel announcements seem narrative, not a crisis: three-quarters at 5154, braking at 5394, quarter at 5634, arrival proximity 5874. Hungry AND thirsty warning at command 54, 5874; immediately saved (56) and ate orange goo (57), which tasted of apricot yogurt. Opened Thermos to address thirst next; it contains blue soup. Docked at 6114 and earned 5 points. No welcoming crew. This establishes an empty-station mystery rather than a straightforward delivery.
- Arrival layout: "In the center is the large, spherical Command Module. Jutting "north" from it is a smaller Sub-Module. Joining the Command Module, at its two other connection points, is a tangle of tubes and space bubbles and derelict rockets. These form a "village," the sort of seedy, unauthorized village that frequently collects around a space station."
- Warning at 5874: "A growl from your stomach warns that you're getting pretty hungry and thirsty." "(Come to think of it, you haven't seen much food on this station. Whatever you find may have to last you.)"
- Docking recording: "Docking bay one is occupied. Defaulting to bay two." Then "Stationfall." Theory: bay one vessel and missing crew are early investigation targets.
Commands 59–68: Soup refused because I was neither hungry nor thirsty—orange ration satisfies both. The countdown says about 287 moves, but then lists walking ~3, examining ~5, waiting ~6; the units feel unclear. I left the truck and entered Level Five. Floyd initially seemed absent on disembarkation but bounded in after LOOK, so I did not abandon him. Last save command 66, Docking Bay #2, 6164. Lobby offers north, northeast, southeast, up, down, elevator east, bay west. I will begin north rather than attempt machinery with no context.
- Soup refusal: "You're neither hungry nor thirsty." "(You'll be able to eat once you are hungry, in about 287 moves: walk ~3, examine ~5, wait ~6.)"
- Floyd at 6195: "Floyd here now!"
Commands 69–78: Workshop north of lobby contains twenty-ohm bedistor, which I took as a deliberately singled-out puzzle component. Machinery itself is decorative/inaccessible to my character expertise. North of Workshop is dark Storage, so I immediately retreated south rather than tempt the explicit grue warning. Need a light. Last save command 76, Workshop, 6263. This is a clean gating mechanism if a lamp is reasonably discoverable; no reason to brute-force darkness. Next I will inspect the lobby corridors and find inhabited spaces or supplies.
- Workshop machinery: "Since this equipment has nothing to do with the filling out or filing of multi-part forms, it's far outside your area of expertise."
- Storage: "It is pitch black. You hope there are no grues aboard the station." Theory: find portable light before returning.
Commands 79–87: Level Five NE reaches North Junction; east reaches Sick Bay. There is an east security door and southeast exit. Machinery again gives the same expertise refusal, suggesting background dressing rather than medical help. Examining the reader gives an explicit rank rule. I carry an ID in my uniform, so I will test it after saving. Last save command 84 at North Junction, 6362. No station personnel encountered. Need light, explanation for abandonment, and eventual form validation/cargo. I have not entered the elevator or ladders yet.
- Sick Bay reader: "The ID reader is a featureless black box. It is activated by inserting an ID card into it. An ID of sufficient rank will cause the security door associated with the reader to open." Theory: own ID may work; if not, find higher rank.
- Personal ID reads: "STELLAR PATROL / Paperwork Task Force / ID Number: 1451-352-716" (line breaks shown as slashes here). Insert card produces "Nothing happens." East remains blocked. Theory: insufficient rank rather than broken door, but feedback does not distinguish them.
Commands 88–97: Personal ID failed to open Sick Bay east. I moved SE into East Connection. East is a tight Military Sub-Module iris hatch with slot, southwest unknown, west junction, south Comm Center. Floyd left to explore at 6498. Saved command 96 at East Connection. Comm Center is unstaffed despite round-the-clock regulations; this substantiates concern. Its emergency beacon is plainly marked, so I will save then request help. I am treating the empty station as an emergency, not randomly pressing buttons for score.
- Floyd at 6498: "Floyd going exploring. See you later."
- Comm Center: "Although regulations state that the Comm Center must be monitored around the clock, ten chrons per day, there's no one on duty." "However, the red button of the wide-band emergency beacon is well-marked. Next to the button is a large screen for displaying incoming messages. At the moment, the screen is blank."
- Beacon command 100: "The instant you touch the button, a powerful electric shock makes you jerk back." Investigated immediately with status and DIAGNOSE; command 101: "You feel well-rested, and you are well-fed. In all other respects, you are in good health." Theory: sabotage or electrical fault, protective equipment needed. Do not retry barehanded.
Commands 98–106: Beacon shocked me; diagnosis immediately established no lasting injury. I will need insulation or repair, not repeated pressing. East Connection SW reaches Station Control. Monitors report communication and food production RED, printing YELLOW, life support/gravity/computer/power GREEN. This is a useful overview and raises ration conservation priority. Saved command 104 at East Connection, 6567. Timeline day 1 6596: communications and food down while life support holds. I should seek a log or staff offices explaining when this began.

Commands 107–116: Station Control south leads Commander’s Office; reader fixed there. Plato knows no explanation for crew disappearance ("I was going to ask you the same question!"). Generic station question got a library remark, so broad conversation is not productive. East office door leads quarters, containing safe and log tape on desk. That pairing is fair clue placement: the tape is next door to its player. Last save 115, Office, 6646. I will read tape notation and inspect safe before carrying tape back. Both robots follow.
- Plato about station: "Sorry, I don't know much about that. I'll be sure to see what I can find the next time I'm in the station's library, though."
- Quarters: "A sturdy safe is welded to the deck next to the desk." "Sitting on the Commander's desk is an ordinary-looking log tape. There's a notation printed on it."

Because of the potentially catastrophic effects of a break in the integrity of a hull on the habitat's air supply, hull welders are kept active at all times, roaming around with their sensing devices alert for the tiniest leak." This is a test of the new diode, not a proven solution yet. No status warnings during transit. The extensive preparation makes this attempt feel tense even though the individual menu interactions are clear; I hope the M part resolves the earlier burnout.


### Through reply 1091
Explosive went into the hole for three points, now sixty, and the detonator connected successfully. Timer menu is open. Thirty worked as an escape interval in the earlier failed-diode timeline, so I will use it again and leave west/northwest immediately. No warming or hunger warning has interrupted. This assembly is clearer when the component names remain listed beneath their containers; it is easy to check that explosive is in the hole and not accidentally still in my bottle. The M diode is the only substantive difference from the failed setup.


## Clue log
- Quarters after blast: The safe has been blown open! The area around the safe is blackened, and a burnt odor hangs in the air. It seems that the safe contains a key.
### Through reply 1099
The explosion succeeded; returned to the blackened safe and took key for seven points, score67. Filed a nice friction row for the clear visual-state payoff. Saving now over oldest Chapel slot, preserving the prepared Trading Post recovery. Timer, detonator and explosive consumed. Next Dome locked bin, based on commander log explicitly naming hidden fuel cells there. No current health warning. I feel much closer to leaving, though the corrupted refueling instructions and missing platinum remain unresolved. The good result connects three long object chains into something tangible.


## Clue log
- South Junction after safe: Without warning, the lights flicker and go out, leaving you in the dark! I turned lamp on immediately; station power is worsening.
### Through reply 1107
Saved key progress and climbed toward Dome. The lights failed in South Junction, so I switched on lamp before moving. Its limited life now feels more pressing. No hunger or fatigue warning, and I ignored the known poisoned coffee while passing Mess Hall. Dome is one ladder above. I want the fuel cells before further searching because commander explicitly linked this key and bin. The lamp continues working; no new dimming since airlock. I still carry an empty Thermos that could be dropped if capacity becomes an issue.


## Clue log
- Dome bin: You open the bin, revealing fertilizer, gardening tools, and a supply of fuel cells. Suddenly, the cells explode! The heat and shock toss you halfway across the dome! Your solitary thought before succumbing to unconsciousness is how grateful you are that you landed in such a soft shrub.
- Changed Dome description: Next to the ladder is an air shaft grating, which looks a bit loose.
### Through reply 1115
The fuel exploded instead of providing escape. I immediately diagnosed after unconsciousness: healthy, fed, rested. Take all recovered my dropped inventory. No unwinnable notice, and the loosened grating is an explicit new lead, so I am investigating rather than restoring. This is a disappointing reversal after the long safe chain, but the changed grating signals progress. Latest save remains before the bin explosion. Lamp still on and dimming; no alternate light known. Next examine and open grating.

`n## Clue log`n- P.A. in Air Shaft: "Announcement. Prepare for launch of second-generation pyramids. Station will be eliminated by reactor overload immediately following launch." Need hurry; pyramid reproduction matches the bacteriophage note.

### Through reply 1124
Bent the loose grating and entered for two points, now69. Descending the shaft repeats identical descriptions, making it hard to visualize progress, but the lower choice has finally changed from special to unexplored. The P.A. announced pyramid launch and reactor destruction; I copied it immediately. I am continuing downward because this new route plausibly bypasses the sealed lower ladder. No physiological warning. Lamp still illuminates the duct. I have not assumed fuel explosion made the game unwinnable because it explicitly opened this route and gave points.


## Clue log
- Bottom shaft: (The handholds end here. Whatever is below that grating, there would be no climbing back up from it, so it seems wise to bring everything you might need before going through.) Save before this one-way route; platinum still missing.

## Clue log
- Bottom grating: There's a lighted area below the grating, but you can't see any details.
- Lamp: The light from the headlamp flickers and dies! It is now too dark to see.
- Computer Control: The exercise machine rolls slowly towards you, bellowing, "No pain, no gain!"
- P.A.: "Announcement. Standby. Launch in 200 millichrons."
- Loss notice: (The game can no longer be won: you dropped into Computer Control without the reflective foil. RESTORE your saved position, or start again.)
### Through reply 1132
Saved before grating then looked below; lamp died. Opening dropped me beside hostile exercise machine and declared run unwinnable without reflective foil. This gives a specific missing object, probably platinum-related. Restored latest shaft save, though with about one action of lamp retreat may be impossible. Need find foil before returning. No hunger/fatigue; lamp is immediate danger. Prior diary append failed due quoting; this corrects it.

### Through reply 1140
Climbed all the way back through the dark shaft without attack, following handholds and known exits. Lamp died first move but movement remained possible. Dome is also dark despite the transparent ceiling; I need light before searching for foil. My best is69, current69; latest save remains shaft. I will head toward village where ambient light may remain, and inspect lamp menu for batteries or recharge. The explicit missing-foil notice is my new objective, plausibly connected to platinum detector cached in dark Storage. No physiological warning during retreat. I have not used outside memory.


### Through reply 1148
Reached Main Street in darkness; village lighting also gone. The P.A. repeated launch200 during retreat, so there is little time in this timeline. The lamp appears depleted rather than merely off. I can move safely but cannot inspect room objects, making foil searching impractical. I will inspect its full menus before calling light unrecoverable, then likely restore earlier safe progress to search while lamp remains usable. No hunger or injury warnings. The blacked-out inventory-only panel makes the world's previous visual landmarks disappear, which is effective atmosphere but sharply reduces affordances.


### Through reply 1159
Restored quarters67 because latest shaft state left no light for searches. Re-read diary references to platinum, foil and taffy: no foil recorded, and Shipping had only forms. Went directly to Storage in darkness, conserving lamp until arrival. Turned it on and detector is visible where cached. I will recover and read it carefully, then use short scans to locate reflective material. This is a deliberate new search, not a claim that the foil is in any particular room. Lamp can still run here after restore. No status warning since restoring.


### Through reply 1168
Detector is carried and on, but its examination only reported power state. Walked through north tube into science, now Bio Lab, without any detection response. I chose the labs because a reflective metal might be scientific equipment, an ordinary guess rather than a clue. Lamp remains off in known corridors. I will scan the former pyramid tank and office briefly, then return if silent; no reason to spend scarce light on already-searched generic desks. No hunger, thirst, sleep or injury warning. No detector warming yet in this short run.


### Through reply 1176
Scanned Holding Tank, Bio Office and Engineering Office by walking through with detector on; no signal. Now Astro Lab. I am trying all science rooms systematically before returning, because a silent scan only rules out this particular search, not hidden objects generally. Dark travel remains safe so far. No detector warmth or health warning. The foil may instead be something mundane such as packaging, but my diary recorded no wrapper when taffy was eaten. I will finish upper science and move back to the main station; no reason to keep circling these rooms.


### Through reply 1184
Upper science also gave no detector signal. Returned to North Connection, still dark and no threats. Trying to examine detector in darkness failed, unsurprisingly; I should verify it is genuinely running when next lit rather than assume silent scans mean no platinum. No warmth despite many moves is curious. I will check at PX, then sweep station rooms systematically. Lamp remains conserved. No hunger or tiredness, and no additional launch announcement this loop. I am conscious that repeating dark travel is less engaging than inspecting drawn objects, but it is the available search path under this constraint.


### Through reply 1192
Verified detector is on under lamp at PX, then switched light off again. Scanned Sick Bay, East Connection and Comm Center with no signal. The obvious security door remains closed without ID, so Brig cannot be checked until boots are left and card retrieved. Earlier diary says detector had already been there without finding anything. I am not treating any one scan as exhaustive; it is a way to prioritize scarce light. No health warning. The lamp dimmed again during verification, strengthening the case for brief illumination only at promising objects.


Hunger/thirst warning at reply1197 in South Junction. Interrupting detector search immediately for Greasy Straw nectar; no food carried. No injury or tiredness warning.


### Through reply 1200
Station Control and File Room were silent too. Hunger appeared on leaving File Room; I immediately turned south and now Main Street, one move from nectar counter. I will use a little lamp to reveal it and search. This run has no spare rations, so this known food source is essential. The repeated counter discovery in earlier leg may be repeatable, but I have not proven it in this timeline. Detector remains on, no warming notice. No new clue words or injury warning. Puzzle exploration waits until fed.


### Through reply 1208
Searching counter again produced nectar, and drinking resolved hunger. This is definitely a repeat in the same saved history because the quarters save was after earlier nectar. Turned lamp off immediately afterward. Now Trading Post, ready to scan village branches. I will leave ID untouched while boots are worn. Foil could be in studio materials or shop stock; these are guesses worth checking with the detector. No new health warning after drink. I have not saved over quarters because that remains a useful earlier recovery with more lamp life and time.


## Clue log
- Barbershop: The detector is quietly beeping.
- Mirror examination: It's a standard, old-fashioned glass mirror.
### Through reply 1215
Studio and Grocery silent, but Barbershop finally beeped. Turned on lamp and saw mirror as only distinctive prop. Examination is generic, yet platinum signal gives reason to inspect backing or break glass if menus allow. Detector warmed after this, so switch off now. This successful audible search confirms dark movement can still trigger it. No health warning since nectar. I will inspect every mirror entry before deciding how to recover material. This is the first substantial lead since the safe, and the mirror nicely matches reflected-radiation clue.


### Resume at command 962 — GPT-6
Read diary and existing handoff. Current screen already lists reflective foil where the mirror was, so the previous action evidently exposed it. I will inspect and collect this visible lead before returning to the shaft. Model identity available to me remains GPT-6, matching the existing leg entry; no outside game memory used.
`n## Clue log`n- Barbershop foil examination: "It's a large piece of reflective foil, about two meters on a side." Large enough to cover something or reflect the weapon; take it.

### Through reply 1229
Examined and took the two-meter foil for four points, now71. The visible sheet replaces the mirror, a physical link to the reflected-radiation clue. Saved over the obsolete shaft position, keeping quarters and Trading Post backups. Lamp off for travel; current route Broadway west through connector, then station ladder to Dome. No physiological warning. I am relieved to have a specific missing item rather than continuing a blind scan. The text-only harness still gives no actual picture to inspect. No external game memory used.

Fatigue at reply1234: You begin to feel weary. It might be time to think about finding a nice safe place to sleep. Interrupting Dome trip for nearby barracks bed.

### Through reply 1238
Walked back to Level Four but weariness interrupted. Entered nearby Female Barracks and tried Sleep; darkness hid the bed and the generic Sleep command refused. Turning lamp on exposed the bed and changed Sleep to get in bed. This contextual mismatch is confusing during a health warning, though the light resolved it. I will rest immediately, conserving light as soon as in bed. No injury or hunger warning. The foil save remains safe in Barbershop and I have not spent it on experiments.

### Through reply 1246
Slept until Novem7, woke in darkness, stood and briefly lit the barracks to recover all eight loose possessions. Take all worked neatly. Lamp is off again; foil, key and jammer are secure. Fatigue resolved and no hunger warning followed waking. I filed the bed-in-darkness confusion after fixing UTF8 BOM rejection in the friction input. Next return southwest and climb to Dome. The sleep interruption cost time but follows the explicit warning; no reason yet to restore or assume unwinnable.

### Through reply 1253
Reached Dome but the lamp died immediately on switching on, hiding the bin before I could unlock it. Key and More menus offer no unlock target. Need recover earlier light budget. Barbershop save has very little light left; quarters save gives more if I go directly to mirror and avoid the long detector sweep. I am considering that restore rather than claiming a new light source exists. Fatigue was handled, but sleep's inventory recovery consumed the final light. No current hunger or injury. This feels like a severe click-mode obstacle because known fixtures vanish entirely.

### Through reply 1261
Restored quarters67, then walked directly through Station Control and eastern connector to Barbershop. This avoids detector recovery and the long survey, using only discoveries from the prior timeline. Lamp has stayed off all the way. No fatigue or hunger warning yet after restore. I must expose the foil again; last continuation stopped immediately after that step without recording its verb, so I will inspect mirror and More before acting. The earlier Barbershop save remains a fallback but its lamp is nearly exhausted.
`n## Clue log`n- Breaking Barbershop mirror: "The mirror smashes into a cloud of glass dust, which (fortunately) is quickly sucked away by the barbershop's ventilation system. As the glass is sucked away you discover what gave the mirror its reflectivity: A piece of reflective foil is hanging on the wall where the mirror once was." Break is the required recovery verb.

### Through reply 1271
Mirror More/Break exposed foil; took it and switched lamp off after only three lit actions. Replaced old Barbershop save with this earlier, healthier version. Filed command1000 stocktake, leaving200 commands this leg. Heading west to station now. This replay has a much smaller carrying load because detector stayed in Storage, and should leave more light for bin and grating. No current physiological warning. The mirror recovery is now documented explicitly so another tester need not infer it from a changed object list.

### Through reply 1279
Direct walk reached Dome without fatigue this time. Lamp remains off and no hunger warning. The earlier failure was recoverable by applying what the session taught, though repeated dark corridor travel is tedious. I am now ready to unlock the bin, recover possessions after its known blast, and enter the shaft with foil. Jammer still710 off. I will not spend light on already-recorded decorative descriptions or the poisoned coffee. Barbershop save is earlier than this walk and retains the foil.

### Through reply 1288
Unlocked and opened bin; blast repeated exactly, leaving loose grating. Diagnosed immediately after unconsciousness: well-rested, well-fed, healthy. Recovered all seven loose items, including foil, and bent grating open. Lamp dimmed but remains functional. Next enter and extinguish it during familiar shaft descent; save at bottom with foil this time. I have preserved the efficient Barbershop recovery. No new clue beyond already-copied blast and grating descriptions; no new package-paper numbers.

### Through reply 1296
Entered shaft for two points, best73, then switched lamp off. Descended six times; Down now changes from special to unexplored, indicating the bottom is near. Launch announcement repeated the same copied warning. No hunger, tiredness or injury. I plan to save with foil before the irreversible drop, then inspect the machine under its own room lighting. Jammer frequency710 comes from the gym sign, so that is the first defensive hypothesis. The shaft's identical text still makes counting floors awkward, though the changing exit label helps.
`n## Clue log`n- Computer Control on jammer710: "The exercise machine experiences a series of mechanical spasms and then freezes." / "Before you can catch your breath, a huge, grime-covered forklift descends from the ladder hole on a cushion of anti-gravity. It settles down between the arms of the frozen exercise machine, smoke pouring from its engine vents like steam from the nostrils of an angry bull." Turning jammer off may let arms catch forklift; inference from their positions.

### Through reply 1304
Saved bottom shaft over oldest TradingPost, preserving Barbershop and quarters. Dropped into lit Computer Control with foil; no unwinnable notice this time. Jammer710 froze exercise machine; forklift settled between its arms. Switching jammer off let the arms crush it and both exploded. This was a satisfying visual-position inference from the text, not external memory. Routes north and up now open. No health warning. Launch200 timer is active, so I will follow the ladder promptly.
`n## Clue log`n- Factory: "The original pyramid sits on a pedestal in the center of the factory, like a monarch impassively surveying its domain." / "Floyd is standing between you and the pyramid, his face so contorted by hate as to be almost unrecognizable. You also wonder where he picked up that black eye patch. It seems that Floyd has a stun ray." / "Floyd fires his stun ray nonchalantly in your direction, laughing, as though taunting you. You feel part of your leg go numb." Immediate injury/threat; inspect defense menu first.

### Through reply 1312
Factory reached for two points,75. Floyd is hostile and shot my leg numb, so immediate defense takes priority. Tried foil on pyramid to stop its influence, but Floyd blocks approach. Tried shooting his ray rather than him; game says impossible without hitting Floyd. This is emotionally unpleasant after earlier friendship, and I want to inspect his conversation/menu before taking that drastic step. Reactor light has turned red and pod smoke signals imminent launch. No outside memory. Bottom-shaft save gives recovery before these attempts.
`n## Clue log`n- Factory Floyd when asked about himself: "Oh, quit jabbering already." He fires again, leg numb. More offers only Kick, Touch, Smell, Scare, Play with; no obvious disarm.

### Through reply 1319 — victory
Floyd blocked the pyramid and kept shooting. Asking about himself only produced hostility, and shooting his ray was refused because it would hit him. I shot Floyd, then put foil on pyramid. The reflected emissions destroyed it, launch aborted, station systems recovered, and the game explicitly says You have won, score80 day3. Floyd died apologizing; Oliver arrived with the paddleball. This is a sad ending rather than the simple escape I expected. My leg still has budget, so I will check Continue and comply with the harness limit. No external game knowledge used.

## Clue log
- Ending: "Launch aborted -- launch -- abort --"
- Narrator: "The replica pyramids fade to darkness, and a subtle change in background sound tells you that the space station's systems and machinery are returning to their normal functions."
- Floyd: "Floyd sorry for the way he acted. Floyd knows...you did what you...had to do."
- Floyd: "One last game of Hider-and-Seeker? You be It. Ollie ollie..." / "...oxen..." / "...free..."
- Oliver: "Play game... Play game with Oliver?"

Continue confirmed80/80 Intergalactic Mega-Hero and exhausted ending controls. Status237/400,1037total:163commands remain. Because launch explicitly requires whole leg, restoring for systematic untried-route exploration rather than stopping at victory. Victory remains observed and recorded; ending screen no longer offers gameplay.
`n## Clue log`n- Fortune Teller crystal ball: "Tips: Be general with your predictions. Always promise romantic encounters. And wave your hands around the crystal ball; the marks just love that touch." Comic lettering, no practical puzzle procedure.

### Through reply 1330
Post-victory survey from saved Barbershop: visited Fortune Teller and read the crystal-ball lettering, a joke about exploiting customers. Gaze into was a good distinctive menu action; ordinary Examine alone would miss that text. Lamp dimmed, so off again. I am heading toward the untried elevator, which has remained on every hub picture-list while I used ladders. Current score71 after restore, best80 and win preserved in diary. No hunger or fatigue warning. The remaining budget is exploration, not evidence that the ending failed.

### Through reply 1338
Returned to Level Five, lit the lobby and pushed call button. Elevator arrived with warm-air whoosh and the east exit changed to unexplored. This is a clear affordance that I avoided earlier because other machines attacked. With a reliable winning save preserved, I can investigate it now. No health warning. Lamp on for the controls. The rest of station route was unchanged. I am particularly checking whether this provides a useful shortcut or a danger the picture-like object list warns about.
`n## Clue log`n- Elevator entry: "The elevator shaft is supposed to be a weightless environment, outside of the station's artificial gravity field. But the gravity in the shaft is one standard Gee!" This warns against stepping into empty shaft.`n- Elevator: "There is a keypad for typing the number of the level you want to go to." Test a known level.

Elevator keypad3 caused immediate fatal power dive. No health warning could be acted on between selection and death. Restore latest viable shaft save now; do not repeat elevator travel.
`n### Through reply 1348`nRestored bottom shaft and cleared the two machines again. Examined the computer rather than rushing up: description discourages its use, saying even experts need manuals. North remains unexplored and may simply enter the elevator shaft. I will check that next. No health warning since restore. This is an optional post-victory inspection of previously bypassed scenery; I am retaining the proven ending procedure and preserving the shaft save.`n## Clue log`n- Computer: "You may as well ignore the computer -- even computer experts need to consult manuals to understand this model." Explicitly deprioritizes this prop.

### Through reply 1355
North from Computer Control is bottom of elevator shaft, not another escape corridor. Its description says only exit south; Up confirms no climb. Returned, checked computer More and Look behind; same discouraging manual response. These alternatives are now meaningfully tested rather than assumed absent. No physiological warning, lamp off. Next inspect factory pedestal and pyramid menus more carefully, keeping the danger and countdown in mind. I can restore if the timer expires; the existing shaft save still has every winning item.
`n## Clue log`n- Floyd refused drop-ray order: "Shut up!"`n- Pyramid examination: "The pyramid is completely featureless, but you can almost feel the emanations of evil pouring forth from it, urging the surrounding factory on towards its sick and deadly purpose. The pyramid is somewhere between half a meter and a meter across." Two-meter foil easily covers it.`n### Through reply 1363`nChecked Floyd command menu: Drop stun ray exists but he refuses. Defended by shooting him, then Diagnose gave adrenaline rather than injury detail. Examined pyramid and its size matches the foil. This reinforces the physical covering inference that already won. I am inspecting remaining factory surfaces while the threat is neutralized; timer still makes this a temporary survey, not a safe place to idle. No hunger or fatigue warning.

### Through reply 1370
Saved Factory75 before foil and verified that it still wins immediately, despite optional lower-room inspection. This is now the newest proven viable save. Tried restoring Barbershop directly from victory, but pending Hit Enter swallowed Restore and only printed rank80; logged bug. Need invoke restore again after ending prompt dismissed. No new physical warning. Next survey theatre and upper rooms whose props were previously rushed; final Factory save allows ending the leg at victory without replaying all travel.

### Through reply 1378
Restore now worked. Returned via connector to Level Five, lamp off, following familiar route toward theatre. Current timeline is again before fuel blast, no new warnings. I intend to inspect the locked projection booth from its full menu; it was an early spool-reader guess that got abandoned once Library solved reading. Winning did not require it, but unexplored affordances may still reveal useful feedback or visual consistency issues. No code or other session files inspected.

### Through reply 1386
At Theatre, booth examination is generic while Open says closed and locked. Lock has its own menu but no Unlock option, unlike the Dome bin with matching key. I will read lock and both More menus before concluding access unavailable. Lamp dimming repeats known warning; I will leave after this focused inspection. No player hunger/fatigue/injury. The theatre is visually prominent in prose but may just be scenery, which generic menus make difficult to distinguish from real puzzle machinery.

### Through reply 1394
Full booth, lock and key menus supply no unlocking action or lock target. Look behind found nothing. I am leaving that optional prop, lamp off, rather than repeatedly guessing. No health warning. Next check Mess Hall east, still marked unexplored, and remaining meeting-room furniture. The winning state remains safely saved in Factory75 and can be completed with one foil placement. Current score71 is solely because this is a restored exploration branch.

### Through reply 1401
Mess Hall east was elevator already parked here; stepped back without touching fatal keypad. Meeting rooms contain no furniture beyond generic surfaces. Library still has both cached spools, confirming persistent object placement. Its removed computer terminal fits the machine migration story; I did not previously dwell on that detail. Lamp remains on for a brief magazine check, then off. No physiological warning. This loop accounts for the remaining unexplored exit near the Mess Hall and confirms no hidden room beyond it.

### Through reply 1410
After stocktake1100, descended to Male Barracks to resolve special compass directions. South and southeast merely enter uninteresting cubicles and mark tried. This confirms those labels are not new rooms. Library magazines were familiar titles, no new practical clue, and lamp is off again. No hunger or tiredness. I will finish southwest cubicle and the barracks loop, then continue down to printing where the unused mauve spool remains. These are finite checks rather than circling solved machinery.

# Playtest round 17: triage

Generated by `node scripts/playtest-registry.mjs report 17` from playtests/REGISTRY.jsonl and the round's friction JSONL. Do not edit by hand; re-run it.

86 friction rows this round (33 of them praise, counted and not triaged); 53 linked to 39 issues (10 new, 29 repeats); 0 not yet linked.

By tier: 5 A, 5 B, 29 C.

Suggested A/B/C is the registry's guess from the kind (A: build it, B: a deviation for the sponsor, C: leave it as the original). **Norm confirms each one** (`confirm <id> A|B|C`) after checking it against the ZIL and the oracle.

## New issues

| Issue | Title | Area / room | Kind | Rows this round | Rows in all | Rounds | Suggested | Norm confirms | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SF-324 | After the win, Restore sits beside Continue while the final score is held behind [Hit RETURN/ENTER.]; choosing it only releases the score, and the restore is lost | Page / Factory | bug | 1 | 1 | 17 | A | A | fixed | Interface, ours (page and harness alike). The win ends in CONTINUE's "[Hit RETURN/ENTER.]" (rules/library.js:297-298; PYRAMID-F, station.zil 3950-3954), and engine/core.js:780 (zdispatch) gives any next command only the held text. But the end screen offers Restore and Start again beside Continue while text is held (wwwroot/ui/ui.js:403-406, restore2; scripts/lib/playtest-surface.mjs:41-46), so choosing Restore printed the score line and nothing was restored. Seen: r17-illustrator-full commands 1073-1075 (won at 1073; Restore at 1074 printed "Your score is 80..."; the same Restore at 1075 restored).
